sections.markdown:
# Defensive driving, illness, fatigue and aggression

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
Plan realistic travel times instead of attempting to reach an unrealistic destination deadline. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A01
The guide recommends a break to stretch every two hours. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A01
When sharing a trip, the guide recommends changing drivers at two-hour intervals even before feeling tired. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A01
The guide recommends limiting driving during the period from midnight to six in the morning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A01
Difficulty remembering the last few miles is a warning of drowsy driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A01
Repeated yawning, a heavy-feeling head or difficulty keeping the eyes open are drowsiness warnings. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A01
Drifting out of a lane, missing signs or having wandering thoughts can signal fatigue. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A02
An illness or medicine can affect driving even when its effects are temporary. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A02
Some nonprescription cold, allergy or other medicines can cause drowsiness and interfere with driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A02
Read medicine labels for driving-related warnings before taking the product. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A02
Ask a doctor or pharmacist about driving effects when the medicine’s safety is uncertain. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A02
Prescription medicines can affect alertness, vision, judgment or reflexes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A02
A health condition does not automatically mean driving must end; the guide directs seeking medical advice about needed limitations. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A02
Answer licensing questions about physical and mental health honestly when the information can affect driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A02
A Louisiana identification card is an alternative when a person must give up driving privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A03
Aggressive driving includes tailgating, speeding, unsafe lane changes and failing to signal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R17 | anchor: A03
Unsafe passing in front of a truck and repeated lane changes in truck blind spots can create severe danger. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R18 | anchor: A03
Allow enough trip time and avoid driving when angry or exhausted to reduce aggressive behavior. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R19 | anchor: A03
Treat traffic as a situation to respond to courteously rather than a competition to win. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R20 | anchor: A03
When another driver acts aggressively, remain calm, avoid eye contact and leave plenty of space. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R21 | anchor: A03
Move away from an aggressive driver safely rather than challenge the driver by accelerating or defending lane position. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R22 | anchor: A03
Ignore hostile gestures instead of responding to them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R23 | anchor: A03
Do not follow closely or use the horn to punish another driver. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec07-R24 | anchor: A04
If an aggressive driver continues following, go to a police station or a public place with witnesses. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R25 | anchor: A04
Do not drive home when being followed by an aggressive motorist. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R26 | anchor: A04
Do not stop along the roadside to confront a persistent aggressive driver. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R27 | anchor: A04
The guide distinguishes road rage as an escalation into violence, including assault with a vehicle or weapon. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R28 | anchor: A04
Pursuit, deliberate obstruction, intentional vehicle damage or threats can be forms of road-rage behavior. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R29 | anchor: A04
Maintain a safe gap and cooperate with other traffic rather than retaliate after being cut off. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec07-R30 | anchor: A04
Report aggressive driving to law enforcement as soon as possible. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0065]
